newsitem.title: ITALY: European car sales seen down 5.2 pct in Nov - Anfia.
newsitem.headline: European car sales seen down 5.2 pct in Nov - Anfia.

text.p: An 11.4 percent fall in the Italian car market and a 21.7 percent slump in France hit Europe's car market overall in November, cutting new sales by 5.2 percent to 897,500, Italian carmakers' association Anfia said.
But in the January to November period, the European market grew 6.3 percent to 11.93 million new registrations, Anfia said in a statement. Excluding Italy, the rise was 7.5 percent.
Anfia said the fall in the French market was mainly due to a paralysing 12-day truck drivers strike, and also last month the French incentives programme to scrap old cars ended.
In the January-November period, French car sales rose 11.2 percent.
The Spanish market saw an improvement in November with sales up 13.5 percent while Germany saw sales rise a modest 0.6 percent but in Britain sales fell 5.9 percent.
In the January-November period, the Spanish market grew 8.2 percent, Germany rose 5.9 percent and the British market rose 3.8 percent.
